470947699.assessment: Repeated discrete eclipses are present in raw QLP flux; representative event centers give a coherent eclipse period. Fresh independent aperture reduction and source localization are assessed below.
470947699.source: Two fresh detector-sector signed difference stacks favor the target, with free Gaussian offsets and fixed-position capable-neighbour comparisons below. Neighbour capability uses a conservative depth/magnitude threshold; TIC cones extend 60 arcsec. Ratios are descriptive residual comparisons and do not imply calibrated probabilities. Custom TESScut aperture extraction independently recovers the events from the same TESS photons as QLP.
470947699.geometry: Event-derived P=8.170414928 d; Gaia P=8.172049314 +/- 0.001169795 d. Difference -1.40 Gaia sigma is descriptive. Approximate conjunction A offset -0.292 d; covariance linear error 0.225 d; conservative absolute-sum bound 1.171 d. Median fitted duration 3.88 h; approximate central duration 4.59 h. Geometry is physically feasible within approximate radii and propagated orbital phase uncertainty.
470947699.limitations: Representative review; no exhaustive event or sector fits. Independent custom extraction shares TESS photons with QLP. Pixel PRF and catalogue completeness limit astrometry; no formal calibrated PRF significance is claimed.
470947699.next_check: Optional improved spectroscopy and photometry would refine binary characterization.

12320469.assessment: Three sector folds show smooth broad double-wave modulation, without a convincing discrete narrow eclipse. The original screen is refuted as an eclipsing interpretation of this measured signal.
12320469.source: Fresh cutouts were attempted; no established eclipse deficit exists to localize. Source attribution of the smooth modulation is not claimed.
12320469.geometry: The searched modulation period is not an eclipse-derived period. No conjunction comparison is claimed without established eclipses.
12320469.limitations: Smooth modulation may be ellipsoidal or other stellar variability; shallow additional eclipses are not excluded. A local trapezoid fit to a broad trend does not establish an eclipse.
12320469.next_check: Higher precision light curves could test for a narrow residual eclipse if further work on this smooth variable is desired.

201317466.assessment: Deep repeated eclipses are real and coherent. Association with the published Gaia SB1 orbit remains unresolved because its conjunction misses the eclipse by a substantial fraction of a cycle, beyond the conservative linear propagated uncertainty.
201317466.source: Two fresh detector-sector signed difference stacks favor the target, with free Gaussian offsets and fixed-position capable-neighbour comparisons below. Neighbour capability uses a conservative depth/magnitude threshold; TIC cones extend 60 arcsec. Ratios are descriptive residual comparisons and do not imply calibrated probabilities. Custom TESScut aperture extraction independently recovers the events from the same TESS photons as QLP.
201317466.geometry: Event-derived P=5.623860159 d; Gaia P=5.625963779 +/- 0.000558314 d. Difference -3.77 Gaia sigma is descriptive. Approximate conjunction A offset -1.208 d; covariance linear error 0.228 d; conservative absolute-sum bound 0.694 d. Median fitted duration 5.97 h; approximate central duration 7.50 h. Geometry is physically feasible within approximate radii and propagated orbital phase uncertainty.
201317466.limitations: Representative review; no exhaustive event or sector fits. Independent custom extraction shares TESS photons with QLP. Pixel PRF and catalogue completeness limit astrometry; no formal calibrated PRF significance is claimed. Gaia has only 15 RV epochs, modestly constrained eccentricity (0.125 +/- 0.061), and strongly correlated periastron parameters. A 1.208 d conjunction offset versus 0.228 d linear covariance error and 0.694 d conservative sum bound is a physical phase discrepancy; no automatic sigma veto is applied.
201317466.next_check: Refit the RV orbit or evaluate a nonlinear orbital posterior against the observed eclipse timing to resolve Gaia association.

411647453.assessment: Real narrow eclipses contaminate the target aperture, but the proposed target Gaia-period eclipse association is refuted. Two detector sectors place the deficit on nearby TIC 411647413 rather than TIC 411647453. The approximately 0.9151763 d short-period signal gives about seven dips per 6.394568 d screen fold; that screen interval is not a valid target eclipse period.
411647453.source: Sectors11/99 Gaussian deficit centers are 15.09/14.20 arcsec from the target, but 0.56/1.64 arcsec from TIC411647413, separated14.76 arcsec. Fixed neighbour/target SSE ratios are0.362/0.144, consistently favoring that neighbour. A short-period contaminating EB is strongly inferred; its precision ephemeris and novelty were not reviewed.
411647453.geometry: The original conditional 6.394515949 d regression aliased unrelated eclipse dips. It is rejected as an eclipse-derived target period; no Gaia-conjunction association is established.
411647453.limitations: The contaminating eclipses are real; REFUTED applies to target attribution and Gaia-period interpretation. TIC411647413 is an inferred by-catch host subject to pixel model systematics, not a new confirmed catalogue object.
411647453.next_check: Higher resolution event photometry can establish the contaminant host and measure its orbital period precisely.
